tools.name: get_overview
tools.description: Start here. Counts of people, apps and accounts, the total monthly SaaS cost and the alerts an admin should act on (people who left with open accounts, failed removals, connections that need a login).

tools.name: get_spend_by_app
tools.description: Every app with its pricing model, active seats and monthly cost in the company's currency, most expensive first, plus the total.

tools.name: get_app_access
tools.description: Accounts in one app with the person each belongs to (or none: unassigned), role and status, how offboarding removes accounts there and the app's monthly cost.

tools.name: add_app
tools.description: Adds a SaaS app the company pays for. A name the catalog knows ("Notion", "Figma") brings its website, logo and the connector, if there is one. Optional price.

tools.name: update_app
tools.description: Sets the price and pricing model, the admin panel link, category, notes, or who approves access requests for the app (request_policy).

tools.name: find_people
tools.description: Search the company's people (employees and service accounts) by name, e-mail or job title. Each result has the apps the person has an account in and their monthly cost.

tools.name: get_person_access
tools.description: Every open account of one person: app, role, status, monthly cost and how offboarding would remove it (automatic through the app, or a manual task for an admin). Use it to answer 'what does X have?'.

tools.name: list_leavers_with_access
tools.description: People marked as left who still have open accounts in any app: the access a company forgets to remove. Sorted by the number of open accounts.

tools.name: add_person
tools.description: Adds an employee by hand (people usually come from Google Workspace or a CSV import). Creates no accounts: follow with onboard_person or assign_access_profile.

tools.name: update_person
tools.description: Changes job title, department, manager, notes, work e-mail, alias e-mails (other addresses accounts are matched by) or marks the record as a service account. To mark someone as left, use start_offboarding.

tools.name: plan_offboarding
tools.description: What offboarding one person would do, without changing anything: each open account, removed automatically through the app or as a manual task for an admin. Service accounts are skipped. Show this to the user before start_offboarding.

tools.name: start_offboarding
tools.description: Marks the person as left and creates one removal action per open account, all waiting for approval in one batch. Nothing is removed in other apps until approve_actions. Ask the user before calling it.

tools.name: onboard_person
tools.description: Creates accounts for a person in the chosen apps: one creation per app in one batch, waiting for approval. Apps without a connector that can create accounts get a manual task. Ask the user first.

tools.name: list_access_profiles
tools.description: Named sets of apps with roles a role gets ("Developer": GitHub, Slack, Linear), with members, how many miss some access, and the monthly cost per person.

tools.name: assign_access_profile
tools.description: Assigns a profile and creates the missing accounts as one onboarding batch. dry_run (default) only shows what would be created and what it costs.

tools.name: get_access_drift
tools.description: Compares a person's accounts with their access profiles: apps missing, accounts beyond the profiles, roles that differ.

tools.name: list_pending_approvals
tools.description: Every action waiting for an admin's approval, grouped by batch: offboarding removals, onboarding creations, approved access requests.

tools.name: approve_actions
tools.description: Runs the writes of one batch (or of single actions): accounts are really created, removed or suspended in other apps; manual tasks go to the admins. Only after the user said yes to the list.

tools.name: cancel_actions
tools.description: Cancels the actions of a batch (or single actions) that have not finished. Nothing runs in the apps.

tools.name: get_actions_status
tools.description: Status of every action of a batch (pending_approval, approved, running, verifying, done, failed, cancelled) and whether all finished. A failed action has its error.

tools.name: list_open_manual_tasks
tools.description: Approved manual tasks: accounts an admin must create or remove by hand, in apps without a connector or with writes off.

tools.name: complete_manual_task
tools.description: Closes a manual task after the admin did it in the app. Only when the user says it is done: the account is then recorded as removed (or created).

tools.name: list_failed_actions
tools.description: Writes that failed (the app refused, the read-back did not confirm it), with their error.

tools.name: retry_action
tools.description: Reads the app's accounts first (the write may have worked), then runs a failed write again.

tools.name: list_unassigned_accounts
tools.description: Accounts no person is matched to (an e-mail that is not anyone's work or alias e-mail): ex-employees, contractors, shared logins. They cost money and offboarding cannot find them.

tools.name: assign_account
tools.description: Sets who an account belongs to, marks it as a service account (skipped by offboarding) or changes its role. account_id comes from list_unassigned_accounts or get_app_access.

tools.name: add_account
tools.description: Records an existing account in an app without a connector (kept by hand), so it shows in the inventory, costs and offboarding. Does not create anything in the app.

tools.name: list_connectors
tools.description: Every connector with its method (API, SCIM, browser), what it can do (read, create, delete), its settings and which fields are secrets. Read before connect_app.

tools.name: connect_app
tools.description: Saves an app's connection (connector, settings, secrets such as an API or SCIM token) and checks it. Secrets are encrypted and never returned. Writes stay off unless writes_enabled: then offboarding removes accounts in the app automatically.

tools.name: check_connection
tools.description: Tests an app's connection: credentials, a signed-in browser session. Changes no accounts.

tools.name: sync_app
tools.description: Reads the app's account list again in the background (it also runs on a schedule). A sync that would remove more than 30% of the accounts stops; force runs it anyway when the removals are real.

tools.name: get_sync_history
tools.description: The last syncs of an app: status, accounts seen, added and removed, the error of a failed one.

tools.name: list_discovered_apps
tools.description: Third-party apps people signed in to with the company Google account (shadow IT), with the number of users and of users at risk (left, or suspended or deleted in Google). Needs the discovery scan.

tools.name: get_discovered_app_users
tools.description: Every user of one discovered app: e-mail, the matched person, risk (left, suspended, deleted), whether the Google token is still active, and the permissions (scopes) the app holds.

tools.name: track_discovered_app
tools.description: Adds a discovered app to the inventory (or links the app already there) and records its users as accounts, so they show in costs and offboarding.

tools.name: ignore_discovered_app
tools.description: Hides a discovered app the company does not care about (a sign-in helper, a free tool).

tools.name: run_discovery_scan
tools.description: Starts a new scan of the Google Workspace sign-in logs in the background (it also runs daily).

tools.name: list_access_requests
tools.description: Requests for an account in an app ("I need Figma"), from Slack, the panel or an assistant: who, which app, the justification and whose decision they wait for.

tools.name: decide_access_request
tools.description: The admin's decision on a request (also overriding a manager who has not decided). Approval creates the account creation action. Only on the user's word.

tools.name: get_audit_log
tools.description: The append-only audit log, newest first: every change in Open Revoke with its actor (a panel user, an API token, the system), filtered by person, app or text.

tools.name: get_my_access
tools.description: Your own accounts in the company's apps, your open requests and the apps you can ask for.

tools.name: request_access
tools.description: Asks for an account in an app, for yourself or for one of your reports. The app's policy decides who approves: your manager, an admin, both or nobody.

tools.name: list_my_approvals
tools.description: Access requests of your reports that wait for your decision as their manager.

tools.name: decide_my_approval
tools.description: Your decision as the manager on one access request. Only on the user's word.

findings.title: Description issues instructions to the model
findings.detail: Description of "start_offboarding" contains imperative instructions directed at the AI assistant rather than describing the tool. This is the core tool-poisoning technique.

findings.remediation: Treat the server as untrusted; the model may obey embedded instructions.
